models.title: Benjamini-Hochberg critical value at a supplied ordered rank
models.summary: The BH step-up critical line scales the chosen FDR level by ordered rank over complete family size.

relationship.locator: Learning Module6, Multiple Tests and Significance Interpretation, printed pp370-372 (PDF pp380-382), displayed rank criterion and Exhibits12,14
relationship.translation_notes: All quantities are dimensionless. The alpha port is a targetFDR rather than an observation probability. No automatic multiple-test decision is returned, and a single failed comparison does not imply stopping the step-up search.

variables.context: One prespecified complete family of mtests and ascendingly ordered p-values

variables.definition: Integer ordered rank1..m; p-values sorted ascending externally
Positive integer total number of hypotheses in the prespecified family
variables.context: Same complete testfamily,including unreported nonsignificant tests

variables.definition: Rank-specific probability threshold,not an adjusted p-value

assumptions: Rank and family size are integers with1<=rank<=tests; all p-values belong to one prespecified complete testfamily.
FDR control needs the appropriate independent/positive-dependence assumptions of BH; arbitrary dependent families need a qualified alternative.
limitations: Sorting, selecting the largest passing rank, and rejecting all ranks up to that index are separate algorithmic steps,not performed here.
CFA calls these adjusted p-values in Exhibit14; they are critical values.
FDR is expected false discoveries among rejections,not the unconditional per-test false-positive probability.
